name: VFS (Virtual Filesystem Switch)
description: Kernel layer abstracting concrete filesystems (ext4, xfs, btrfs, tmpfs, NFS, etc.) behind a uniform API. Every syscall (open, read, write, stat, mount) goes through VFS. Per-FS modules implement vfs_ops. Concepts: superblock (per-mount), inode (per-file), dentry (path component cache), file (per-open).

name: Inode
description: Per-file metadata structure: mode, uid/gid, size, timestamps (atime/mtime/ctime), block addresses, link count, device. Doesn't include filename (that's in dentry). Number reused after delete. ls -i shows inode number; df -i tracks inode usage (filesystems can run out of inodes before bytes).

name: Dentry (directory entry)
description: VFS cache mapping a name to an inode within a directory. Speeds up path resolution. dcache size visible via slabtop. Negative dentries cache 'this name doesn't exist' for failed lookups.

name: Superblock
description: Per-filesystem metadata: filesystem type, block size, total blocks, free blocks, mount options, magic number. Read on mount, written on superblock-changing ops + sync. Backup copies in ext4 (mke2fs -n shows locations) for recovery.

name: File handle / file descriptor
description: Per-process integer (FD) referencing an open file via the per-process FD table → file struct → inode. Limit per-process by RLIMIT_NOFILE; system-wide by fs.file-max. lsof lists.

name: Path resolution
description: How kernel walks /a/b/c: starts at root (or CWD for relative), looks up 'a' in root's dentry, descends, etc. Symlinks followed up to MAXSYMLINKS (40). Crosses mountpoints. Mount-namespace isolation means 'absolute path' depends on which namespace.

name: mount(2) syscall
description: Attach a filesystem to a path. Args: source, target, fs-type, flags (MS_*), data (fs-specific options). Requires CAP_SYS_ADMIN (or be in user namespace owning the mountns). Modern interface: open_tree(2), fsopen(2), fsmount(2), move_mount(2), fspick(2) for finer control.

name: umount(2) / umount2(2) syscall
description: Detach filesystem. EBUSY if files in use; umount2 with MNT_FORCE for unkillable mounts; MNT_DETACH for lazy unmount (returns immediately, actually detaches when last use closes).

name: open(2) / openat(2) syscall
description: Open a file, returning FD. Flags: O_RDONLY/O_WRONLY/O_RDWR; O_CREAT (create if missing — needs mode), O_EXCL (fail if exists with O_CREAT), O_TRUNC, O_APPEND, O_NONBLOCK, O_SYNC, O_DIRECT, O_NOFOLLOW, O_CLOEXEC. openat takes dirfd + relative path.

name: openat2(2) syscall
description: Modern open with explicit how struct: flags + mode + RESOLVE_* bits (RESOLVE_NO_XDEV, RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS, RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS, RESOLVE_BENEATH, RESOLVE_IN_ROOT, RESOLVE_CACHED). Designed for safe path-resolution in untrusted contexts (containers, sandboxes).

name: stat(2)/fstat/lstat/fstatat
description: Get file metadata. stat follows symlinks; lstat doesn't; fstat takes FD; fstatat takes dirfd + path + AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW flag. Returns struct stat with all inode fields. statx(2) is the modern enriched version.

name: statfs(2)/fstatfs/statvfs
description: Get FILESYSTEM stats: type, block size, total/free/avail blocks/files, fsid. statfs vs statvfs differ slightly in struct layout. The data behind df.

name: fsync(2)/fdatasync/syncfs
description: Force writeback of cached writes for an FD (fsync = data + metadata; fdatasync = data + critical metadata; syncfs = entire filesystem). Required for crash-consistent data. Slow on rotational disks; modern flash much faster.

name: mmap memory mappings
description: Map file pages into process address space. PROT_READ/WRITE/EXEC; MAP_SHARED (changes write back to file) vs MAP_PRIVATE (COW). MAP_ANONYMOUS for anon (heap-style) memory not backed by file. /proc/<pid>/maps lists.

name: Symbolic link
description: File whose contents are a path string. Path resolution follows symlinks (up to MAXSYMLINKS=40). Crosses filesystems. Created by symlink(2) / ln -s. Read by readlink(2). Stat (vs lstat) follows.

name: Hard link
description: Multiple directory entries referring to the same inode. Inode link count = number of hard links. File 'deleted' only when count reaches 0 AND no FDs open. Doesn't cross filesystems. Created by link(2) / ln (no -s).

name: Bind mount
description: Make a path visible at another path (mount --bind src dst). Same inode reachable via two paths. Used by container runtimes for volume mounts. Recursive variant: --rbind. mount(8) + MS_BIND flag.

name: tmpfs
description: In-memory filesystem. Backed by VM (page cache + swap). Sized via mount option size=N (default ~50% RAM). Cleared on unmount/reboot. /tmp, /run, /dev/shm typically tmpfs on modern systems.

name: procfs (/proc)
description: Pseudo-filesystem exposing kernel and per-process info. Not real files — generated on read. /proc/N/* per process; /proc/sys/* sysctls; /proc/net/* network state; /proc/cpuinfo/meminfo/stat etc. The kernel-introspection backbone.

name: sysfs (/sys)
description: Pseudo-filesystem exposing kernel objects (devices, drivers, classes, buses, modules). /sys/class/net/, /sys/block/, /sys/devices/. Many writable for runtime tuning (sysfs interface vs sysctl interface).

name: devtmpfs
description: Pseudo-fs at /dev. Auto-populates device nodes on hotplug events from kernel. Replaces older udev-managed /dev with an in-kernel base layer (udev still adds symlinks/persistent names on top).

name: cgroupfs (/sys/fs/cgroup)
description: Pseudo-fs interface to the cgroup subsystem. Mount of type 'cgroup2' (v2) or 'cgroup' (v1, per-controller). Read/write cgroup.* files to manage. (Concept fully covered in linux/primitives.)

name: bpffs (/sys/fs/bpf)
description: Pseudo-fs for pinning BPF objects (programs, maps, links). Allows objects to outlive the loading process. mount -t bpf bpffs /sys/fs/bpf.

name: FUSE (Filesystem in Userspace)
description: Bridge that lets userspace processes implement filesystems. Kernel module + libfuse. Used by sshfs, ntfs-3g, gvfs, mergerfs. Performance penalty vs native; correctness flexibility wins for many use cases.

name: ext4
description: Default Linux filesystem since ~2010. Extents (vs ext3 block-mapped), delayed allocation, journaling (data=ordered/writeback/journal modes), 1 EiB max FS size. Mature, stable, well-understood. mkfs.ext4, tune2fs, e2fsck.

name: XFS
description: High-performance scaling filesystem. Allocation groups for parallelism; B+tree indexed. 8 EiB max. Strong on large files + parallel IO. Less common for /, common for /var or /data on busy servers. mkfs.xfs, xfs_repair, xfs_growfs.

name: Btrfs
description: Copy-on-write filesystem with snapshots, subvolumes, RAID, integrity (checksums + scrub), online resize. Heavy in Fedora workstations and openSUSE. Reputation: amazing-when-it-works, painful-when-it-doesn't (esp. RAID5/6).

name: OverlayFS
description: Union mount: stack a writable upperdir on top of one or more read-only lowerdirs. Reads check upper then lower; writes go to upper (with copy-up). The mechanism behind every modern container's image-layer + writable-layer model. Mount type 'overlay' with options lowerdir=,upperdir=,workdir=.

name: OverlayFS lowerdir
description: Read-only base layer(s). Multiple : separated. First (leftmost) wins for files present in multiple. Container images: each layer is one lowerdir.

name: OverlayFS upperdir
description: Read-write top layer where modifications go. Container 'writable layer'. Empty initially.

name: OverlayFS workdir
description: Empty dir on same FS as upperdir. Used internally for atomic operations (rename for copy-up). User shouldn't touch.

name: OverlayFS copy-up
description: On first write to a lower-only file, the file is copied to upperdir then modified. Subsequent reads/writes use upper. Slow on large files (entire file copied even for small change).

name: OverlayFS whiteout
description: Special character device (mode 0, major:minor 0:0) in upperdir marking a lower file as deleted. Lookup returns ENOENT. Visible via ls -la in upperdir but invisible in merged view.

name: ramfs
description: Simpler than tmpfs — no swap backing, no size limit (will eat RAM until OOM). Used internally for initial rootfs (rootfs is ramfs-with-no-mount-namespace), early initramfs.

name: initramfs
description: Initial RAM-disk filesystem the kernel mounts as rootfs at boot. cpio archive embedded in or alongside kernel; loaded into ramfs. Init script switches to real root via switch_root. Distros use dracut, mkinitcpio, initramfs-tools to generate.

name: LVM (Logical Volume Manager)
description: Layer between block devices and filesystems: PV (physical volume) → VG (volume group) → LV (logical volume). Lets you resize, snapshot, mirror, stripe across underlying disks dynamically. lvm/pvcreate/vgcreate/lvcreate.

name: LVM snapshot
description: COW snapshot of an LV at a point in time. Initially shares all blocks with origin; only changed blocks consume snapshot space. Used for backups (snapshot, dump from snapshot, drop snapshot). Thin snapshots (thin pool) are common in modern setups.

name: dm-crypt / LUKS
description: Block-level encryption. cryptsetup luksFormat creates LUKS header + sets up key slots. luksOpen creates /dev/mapper/<name> mapped device. Filesystem mounted on top. Used for full-disk encryption.

name: Loop device
description: Block device backed by a regular file. losetup -f assigns a /dev/loopN; -d detaches. Used to mount disk images, raw container images, encrypted containers.

name: Block device
description: Disk-like device exposed via /dev/<name> (sda, nvme0n1, vda). Read/write in blocks (typically 512B or 4K). Major:minor identifies driver+instance. lsblk shows hierarchy.

name: Disk partition
description: Logical subdivision of a disk. MBR (legacy, 4 primary + extended, 2TB max) or GPT (modern, 128 partitions, multi-PB). Each appears as /dev/<diskN><part> (sda1, nvme0n1p2). Tools: fdisk/gdisk/parted/sfdisk.

name: Filesystem UUID
description: 128-bit identifier in superblock. Used in /etc/fstab as `UUID=...` so mounts work regardless of /dev/sdaN renumbering. blkid lists; tune2fs -U / xfs_admin -U change.

name: Filesystem label
description: Human-readable name in superblock. Same role as UUID for mounting (LABEL=root in fstab). Limited length per FS (ext4: 16 chars; xfs: 12). e2label / xfs_admin -L.

name: Mountpoint
description: Directory where a filesystem is attached. Original contents become hidden until unmount. Modern systemd unit name = encoded path (var-lib-foo.mount).

name: /etc/fstab
description: Boot-time mount declarations. 6 fields per line: device, mountpoint, fstype, options, dump-frequency, pass-order. systemd auto-generates .mount units from this. Edit with care — broken fstab can prevent boot.

name: /etc/mtab and /proc/mounts vs /proc/self/mountinfo
description: /etc/mtab: legacy text file (now usually symlink to /proc/mounts). /proc/mounts: kernel's view of host's mountns (via /proc/self/mounts). /proc/self/mountinfo: per-process mount-namespace view with full per-mount detail (id, parent, optional fields, propagation type) — what container debugging needs.

name: POSIX ACL
description: Per-file extension to DAC mode bits, stored in xattrs (system.posix_acl_access, system.posix_acl_default). Per-user / per-group permissions beyond owner/group/other. Mask entry caps named entries. getfacl/setfacl tools.

name: Extended attributes (xattr)
description: Per-file key-value metadata. Namespaces: user.* (free), system.* (kernel uses for ACLs, etc.), security.* (SELinux/IMA/file caps), trusted.* (root-only). getfattr/setfattr tools.

name: inotify
description: Per-watch filesystem event notification. inotify_init1, inotify_add_watch, read events from FD. Watches don't follow symlinks; can't watch entire subtrees recursively (must add per-dir). fs.inotify.max_user_watches limits.

name: fanotify
description: More powerful filesystem notification. Recursive (whole-mount or whole-FS scope), can permission-block events (FAN_OPEN_PERM), reports PID. Used by AV, file-integrity monitors. Requires CAP_SYS_ADMIN.

name: io_uring
description: Async IO syscall family (5.1+). Two ring buffers shared kernel↔user: submission queue (SQ) for ops, completion queue (CQ) for results. Avoids syscall-per-op overhead. Operations: read, write, fsync, sendmsg, recvmsg, accept, connect, openat, close, etc. The future of async on Linux.

name: O_DIRECT (direct IO)
description: Bypass page cache — IOs go straight from user buffer to disk. Buffers must be aligned (typically 512B); size must be multiple of FS block size. Used by databases that manage their own cache (Oracle, PostgreSQL with effective_io_concurrency, MySQL InnoDB).

name: Sparse file
description: File with 'holes' — regions never written, reported as zeros, take no disk space. Created by seek-past-end + write, or fallocate(2) FALLOC_FL_PUNCH_HOLE. cp --sparse, tar --sparse handle correctly. df shows actual usage; ls shows logical size.

name: Reflink (cp --reflink)
description: Copy-on-write file copy (xfs, btrfs, ocfs2, bcachefs). Source + dest share blocks until one is modified. Constant-time copy regardless of size. cp --reflink=always.

name: Subvolume (btrfs)
description: Independent mountable filesystem-tree within a btrfs filesystem. Has own seed/inode space. Snapshotted independently. Used for installer rollback (snapper), per-container rootfs (podman btrfs driver).

name: Journaling
description: Write-ahead log of metadata (and optionally data) changes. On crash, replay journal to bring FS to consistent state. ext3/ext4: data=writeback (no data, fastest, weakest), data=ordered (data before metadata, default), data=journal (full data journal, slowest). XFS: metadata-only journal.

name: Filesystem quotas
description: Per-user/per-group/per-project block + inode limits. Soft limit (warning + grace period) + hard limit. quotaon enables; edquota edits; quotacheck rebuilds. XFS has built-in (no quotacheck needed), ext4 needs quota mount option.

name: Filesystem state: clean
description: Successfully unmounted; no replay needed on next mount. Tracked in superblock (ext4 s_state has EXT4_VALID_FS).

name: Filesystem state: dirty
description: Mounted (or wasn't unmounted cleanly). On next mount, journal replay runs (ext4) or fsck must run (non-journaled fs).

name: Filesystem state: error
description: Kernel detected corruption (bad block read, inconsistent metadata) and marked FS errored. errors=remount-ro (default for ext4) remounts RO; errors=panic crashes; errors=continue logs and continues. Read superblock with tune2fs -l.

name: Mount state: mounted
description: Active mount. Visible in /proc/mounts and findmnt.

name: Mount state: busy (EBUSY)
description: umount returns EBUSY when files open / processes have CWD inside / active sub-mount. lsof / fuser identifies blockers. umount -l (lazy) detaches anyway.

name: Filesystem auto-remounted RO
description: errors=remount-ro triggered. Symptoms: writes fail with EROFS. Common after disk errors, RAID degradation. Diagnose: `mount | grep ro,`; `dmesg | grep -i 'EXT4-fs error'`. Fix: unmount, fsck, remount.

name: /proc/<pid>/fd/
description: Symlinks per open FD pointing to file/socket/pipe/etc. ls -l reveals what's open. Crucial for debugging FD leaks, finding deleted-but-held files.

name: /proc/<pid>/maps
description: VMAs of process: address-range, perms (rwxp), offset, dev:inode, path. Shows mmap'd files, shared libraries, heap, stack, [vdso], [vsyscall].

name: /proc/<pid>/mountinfo
description: Per-process-mountns mount table with full detail. Format: mount-id parent-id major:minor root mountpoint mount-options optional-fields - fs-type source super-options. Source of findmnt's data.

name: /proc/<pid>/mountstats
description: Per-mount stats (esp. for NFS): bytes-read/written, RPC counts, latency histograms.

name: /proc/diskstats
description: Per-block-device IO counters: reads/writes (counts, merges, sectors, ms), in-flight, ms-doing-io. The data behind iostat.

name: /proc/mounts
description: Symlink to /proc/self/mounts. Active mounts in current mountns. Source: kernel's mount table.

name: /proc/filesystems
description: Filesystem types the kernel can mount. 'nodev' prefix = no block device required (tmpfs, proc, sysfs).

name: /dev/<disk> block device nodes
description: Per-disk device node. /dev/sda for SATA/SCSI; /dev/nvme0n1 for NVMe; /dev/vda for virtio. Created by devtmpfs at boot, persistent symlinks added by udev (/dev/disk/by-uuid/, by-label/, by-id/, by-path/).

name: /sys/block/<disk>/
description: sysfs interface to block device — queue/* tunables (scheduler, nr_requests, read_ahead_kb), device/model, size, removable. Writable for runtime tuning.

name: /sys/class/net/<iface>/
description: sysfs per-interface (cross-ref linux/networking — mostly there). Mode/MTU/MAC/operstate/statistics writable + readable.

name: discard / TRIM
description: Tell SSD which blocks are no longer in use (FITRIM ioctl, mount option discard, fstrim(8)). SSD wear-leveling benefits. Modern: weekly fstrim.timer (instead of mount discard which is per-delete = lots of small TRIMs).

name: fscrypt (filesystem-level encryption)
description: Per-directory transparent encryption (ext4/f2fs/ubifs). Different from dm-crypt: one FS, multiple encryption policies; integrates with kernel keyring. Used by Android/ChromeOS.

name: Recursive bind mount (rbind)
description: mount --rbind src dst — bind src AND all its sub-mounts at dst. Container runtimes use this for host-fs passthrough. Without -r, only src itself is bound (sub-mounts invisible at dst).

name: Mount peer group
description: Mounts in same propagation peer group share events (when one mounts/unmounts, others see it). Created via MS_SHARED. Distinct from MS_PRIVATE/SLAVE/UNBINDABLE. (Cross-ref linux/primitives mount-namespace-propagation.)

name: Mount ID
description: Per-mount unique integer (rotates after umount). Visible in /proc/self/mountinfo first column. Useful for distinguishing two mounts of same FS at different points.

name: Extended file attributes (chattr)
description: Per-file attribute bits. ext4: i (immutable — can't modify/delete even by root), a (append-only), A (no atime updates), S (sync), j (journal data), c (compress). chattr +i / lsattr.

name: umask
description: Per-process bitmask removed from new file/dir mode. Default 022 → files 644, dirs 755. Set per-shell (umask command), per-systemd-service (UMask= directive), per-PAM (pam_umask).

name: Access time modes (atime/relatime/noatime)
description: strictatime: every read updates atime (slow). relatime (default): atime updated only if older than mtime/ctime or > 24h. noatime: never. nodiratime: only files. Mount options.

name: fanotify permission events
description: FAN_OPEN_PERM/FAN_ACCESS_PERM — kernel suspends syscall, asks userspace listener (FAN_ALLOW or FAN_DENY). Used by AV scanning. Process blocked until response.

name: LUKS header
description: On-disk header for cryptsetup. Holds master-key encrypted by per-keyslot passphrases (8 slots LUKS1; 32 slots LUKS2). luksDump shows slots + cipher + KDF.

name: bcachefs
description: Newer COW filesystem (mainlined 6.7). Snapshots, native multi-device, encryption, compression. Still maturing — production-ready debate ongoing. Not in our focus corpus.

name: ZFS
description: Out-of-tree filesystem (CDDL license incompatible with GPL). OpenZFS Linux port (ZoL) widely used for storage servers. Pool-based: zpool/zfs commands. Not a kernel-tree FS but ubiquitous in storage/Proxmox setups.

name: squashfs
description: Read-only compressed filesystem. Used for live-distro ISOs, container image layers (podman/docker overlay2 stores layer tars; some other tools use squashfs directly). mksquashfs creates.

name: NFS (Network File System)
description: Network filesystem. v3 (stateless, UDP/TCP), v4 (stateful, TCP, idmap, ACLs, delegations). mount -t nfs server:/path /mount. Common D-state-stuck culprit when server unreachable. nfsstat for stats.

name: CIFS / SMB
description: Windows network FS. mount -t cifs //server/share /mount -o username=. cifs.ko or ksmbd.ko (in-kernel server).

name: ext2 / ext3
description: Predecessors of ext4. ext2 = no journal; ext3 = added journal. Modern systems mount as ext4 (ext4 driver handles all three formats). Still seen on /boot or USB drives.

name: Disk image (raw, qcow2, vmdk)
description: File representing a block device. raw = sparse file = direct dd. qcow2 = QEMU's COW format with snapshots, compression, encryption. vmdk = VMware. Mountable via losetup or qemu-nbd.

name: device-mapper (dm)
description: Kernel block-layer mechanism for stacking transformations: dm-linear (LVM linear), dm-stripe (LVM stripe), dm-mirror, dm-crypt (LUKS), dm-thin (thin pool), dm-cache, dm-snapshot, dm-multipath. /dev/mapper/<name>. dmsetup CLI.
